issues.legal_issue: A concurrent factual finding that a family belonged to the Sudra community is not disturbed on appeal without sufficient reason.
material_facts: Both lower courts found that the parties belonged to the Sudra community.
The finding was largely based on oral evidence, and the appellate court had considered the applicable tests for distinguishing the communities.
The Supreme Court found no good reason to depart from its practice of not disturbing concurrent findings.
issues.conclusion: The concurrent finding that the parties belonged to the Sudra community was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: The Court follows the established practice of not disturbing concurrent findings of fact by the trial court and the first appellate court when there is no good reason to do so.

rule.if: civil_appeal and concurrent_factual_finding and oral_evidence_supports_finding and relevant_tests_considered and no_sufficient_reason_to_interfere

predicates.civil_appeal: The matter is a civil appeal from a lower-court decision.
predicates.concurrent_factual_finding: The trial court and first appellate court reached the same factual finding.
predicates.oral_evidence_supports_finding: Oral evidence supports the factual finding.
predicates.relevant_tests_considered: The appellate court considered the applicable tests for making the finding.
predicates.no_sufficient_reason_to_interfere: No sufficient reason is shown for disturbing the concurrent finding.

issues.definition: When a civil appeal challenges a concurrent factual finding supported by oral evidence and reached after considering the relevant tests, and there is no sufficient reason to interfere, the finding is upheld.

issues.legal_issue: A father who lived separately from his brother and whose property and produce were dealt with by separate shares was separate in status from his brother despite the absence of a division by metes and bounds.
material_facts: The brothers lived in separate houses and were said by witnesses to have separate households.
Evidence showed that produce was divided between them and that accounts of their respective shares were to be adjusted.
The court found that the evidence established separation in status even though the properties had not been divided by metes and bounds.
issues.conclusion: The finding that the father was separate from his brother was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: Separation in status may be established by evidence of separate living and dealings with property according to defined shares; a physical division of property by metes and bounds is not essential to establish that status.

rule.if: civil_appeal and dispute_over_family_separation and separate_residences and property_enjoyed_by_shares and evidence_supports_separate_status

predicates.civil_appeal: The matter is a civil appeal.
predicates.dispute_over_family_separation: The parties dispute whether family members were joint or separate.
predicates.separate_residences: The family members lived in separate residences.
predicates.property_enjoyed_by_shares: The family members received or accounted for produce or income according to separate shares.
predicates.evidence_supports_separate_status: The evidence as a whole supports separation in status.

issues.definition: In a civil appeal disputing family separation, separate residences, enjoyment of property by shares, and supporting evidence lead to a finding of separation in status.

issues.legal_issue: An illegitimate son of a Sudra may enforce partition after his father's death when the father was separate from his collaterals and left separate property and legitimate sons.
material_facts: The claimant was found to be an illegitimate son of a Sudra.
The father had died, was found separate from his brother, and had left separate property and legitimate sons.
The claimant sought partition of the property left by his father.
issues.conclusion: The claimant was entitled to enforce partition against the legitimate sons in respect of the separate property left by his father; an illegitimate son takes one-half of the share that a legitimate son would take on partition.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the Mitakshara, Chapter 1, section 12, and the Privy Council decision in Vellaiyappa v. Natarajan, AIR 1931 PC 294. An illegitimate son of a Sudra has the status of a son; he acquires no interest by birth and cannot demand partition during his father's lifetime. After the father's death, he succeeds as a coparcener to the father's separate estate with legitimate sons and may enforce partition, taking half the share of a legitimate son. Where the father left no separate property and no legitimate son and was joint with collaterals, the illegitimate son is entitled to maintenance from the joint property, not partition.

rule.if: partition_suit and claimant_is_sudra_fathers_illegitimate_son and father_has_died and father_was_separate_from_collaterals and father_left_separate_property and father_left_legitimate_sons

predicates.partition_suit: The proceeding is a suit seeking partition of property.
predicates.claimant_is_sudra_fathers_illegitimate_s: The claimant is the illegitimate son of a father who belonged to the Sudra community.
predicates.father_was_separate_from_collaterals: The father was separate in status from his collateral relatives.
predicates.father_left_separate_property: The father left property that was his separate estate.
predicates.father_left_legitimate_sons: The father left one or more legitimate sons.

issues.definition: In a partition suit, an illegitimate son of a Sudra father who has died may enforce partition when the father was separate from collaterals and left separate property and legitimate sons.

issues.legal_issue: A co-sharer who is not in possession may maintain a suit for partition unless exclusion and ouster are pleaded and proved.
material_facts: The claimant was a co-sharer in the properties sought to be partitioned.
The claimant was alleged not to be in possession.
Exclusion and ouster were neither pleaded nor proved.
issues.conclusion: The claimant could maintain the partition suit despite not being in possession.
issues.legal_principle: A co-sharer is entitled to partition despite lack of possession unless exclusion and ouster are pleaded and proved.

rule.if: partition_suit and claimant_is_coshareholder and claimant_not_in_possession and not exclusion_and_ouster_pleaded_and_proved

predicates.partition_suit: The proceeding is a suit seeking partition of property.
predicates.claimant_is_coshareholder: The claimant holds a co-ownership share in the property.
predicates.claimant_not_in_possession: The claimant is not in possession of the property.
predicates.exclusion_and_ouster_pleaded_and_proved: Exclusion from the property and ouster of the claimant have both been pleaded and proved.

issues.definition: A co-sharer out of possession may maintain a partition suit when exclusion and ouster have not both been pleaded and proved.

issues.legal_issue: A partition decree must limit a claimant's share to the property categories in which that claimant asserted an interest.
material_facts: A claimant asserted a share in certain categories of property and disclaimed any interest in the other categories.
The claimant's counsel confirmed that the claimant had no claim to the other categories.
The decree therefore required modification to confine that claimant's share to the categories claimed.
issues.conclusion: The decree was modified so that the claimant was entitled to a share only in the property categories in which an interest had been claimed.
issues.legal_principle: The Court gave effect to the claimant's written position as clarified by counsel and modified the decree to conform the claimant's entitlement to the scope of the claim.

predicates.partition_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning a partition decree.
predicates.claimant_claim_limited_to_some_property_: The claimant asserted an interest in only some categories of the disputed property.
predicates.claimant_disclaims_interest_in_other_cat: The claimant disclaimed an interest in the other categories of property.

issues.definition: In a partition appeal, when a claimant's claim is limited to some property categories and the claimant disclaims interest in the others, the claimant's share is limited to the categories claimed.
